final_answer: Antibiotic resistance arises through evolutionary mechanisms such as mutation and natural selection. When bacteria encounter antibiotics, those with genetic mutations that confer resistance survive and reproduce, passing on these traits to subsequent generations. Overprescription accelerates this process by increasing the frequency of antibiotic exposure, thereby enhancing the selection pressure that favors resistant strains. This leads to a higher prevalence of drug-resistant bacteria over time.
